sections.heading: What is Gross Revenue Retention (GRR)?
paragraphs: Gross Revenue Retention (GRR) measures the percentage of recurring revenue retained from existing customers , accounting only for churn and contractions, not expansion.

Unlike NRR, GRR cannot exceed 100% and reveals the true impact of churn without expansion revenue masking problems. A healthy SaaS business should retain 85-95% of recurring revenue year-over-year, with best-in-class achieving 95-100%.

bullets.label: Reveals True Churn Impact
bullets.text: Unlike NRR, expansion can't hide retention problems in GRR

bullets.label: Customer Stickiness
bullets.text: High GRR indicates customers see lasting value and renew contracts

bullets.label: Investor Focus
bullets.text: VCs use GRR to spot churn issues in high-growth companies

bullets.label: Long-term Health
bullets.text: Predicts sustainable growth through customer loyalty

sections.heading: How to Calculate GRR: The Formula
paragraphs: For example, with $100 starting MRR , $5,000 contraction , and $5,000 churn :
sections.formula: GRR = (Starting MRR - Contraction - Churn) / Starting MRR × 100

bullets.text: Critical. Severe churn problem affecting growth potential

sections.heading: GRR by Average Contract Value (ACV)
paragraphs: Higher ACV correlates with higher GRR due to stickier enterprise deals.

sections.heading: GRR vs NRR: Key Differences
paragraphs: Why track both: If NRR is 110% but GRR is 75%, expansion is masking a serious churn problem. Strong companies have high GRR AND high NRR.

bullets.text: GRR Excludes expansion, max 100%, shows true retention
NRR Includes expansion, can exceed 100%, shows growth potential

bullets.label: Improve Onboarding
bullets.text: Get customers to value faster to prevent early churn

bullets.label: Invest in Customer Success
bullets.text: 1-2% of revenue in CS drives measurable retention gains

bullets.label: Fix Cancel Flow
bullets.text: Implement pause walls, trial extensions, and win-back offers
